newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates closes down, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates closes down, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished slightly lower on Friday despite the central bank issued T$8 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit to absorb excess funds, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate finished at 5.680 against Thursday's 5.687 close -- only slightly above the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent, with 30-day commercial paper sliding to 5.35-5.50 against 5.50.
The central bank has said its NCD issue was responding to the banking system's liquidity sitution.
Dealers have expected liquidity to remain loose during the June reserve period that opened on Wednesday.
The central bank's caution over interest rates fluctuations would likely confine the interbank rate at around 5.50-5.75 range next week, dealers said.

In the bond market, the benchmark 86/4 government bond yields, inspired by recent rate cuts by major commercial banks, dipped to a new low at 5.7700 in morning session. But trading interest declined in the afternoon with many investors stepping to the sidelines. -- James Lin (2-5080815)
